analysis.time: The Food and Drug Administration approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine on Wednesday, August 6, 2026, 3:59 AM (N4).
analysis.location_and_population: The vaccine, mFLUSIVA, is expected to be available for people 50 and older in the United States for the 2026-2027 respiratory illness season (N5).
analysis.event: The FDA approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine, which is designed for adults over 50, based on clinical trial results showing a 27% reduction in confirmed flu cases compared to the current standard vaccine (N10).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The vaccine is expected to reduce the risk of severe illness, including hospitalization and death, for people 50 and older (N25). The safety profile was similar to the current standard vaccine, but more people reported mild side effects (N11).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The approval is for the 2026-2027 respiratory illness season, and Moderna will continue to monitor its performance against the high-dose vaccine for those 65 and older (N13). analysis.brief_en: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine, mFLUSIVA, on August 6, 2026, for use in adults over 50. This approval comes after clinical trials showed the vaccine led to 27% fewer confirmed flu cases compared to the current standard vaccine. The safety profile was similar, but more people reported mild side effects. The vaccine is expected to be available for the 2026-2027 respiratory season and may help reduce severe illness, hospitalization, and death in older adults. Moderna plans to monitor its performance against the high-dose vaccine for those 65 and older and submit data to the FDA. The FDA initially stated it would not review the application but reversed its decision after Moderna committed to additional studies. This approval reflects the potential of mRNA technology to address public health challenges through rapid production and adaptability to circulating strains.

title: GSK’s mRNA Flu Vaccine Heads to Phase III - Global Biodefense

analysis.time: GSK announced on Sept. 1, 2026, that it will advance its investigational mRNA seasonal flu vaccine candidate into a pivotal Phase III trial following positive Phase II results presented at the OPTIONS XIII Conference for the Control of Influenza in Washington, D.C. analysis.brief_en: GSK has advanced its investigational mRNA seasonal flu vaccine candidate to Phase III trials following positive Phase II results presented at the OPTIONS XIII Conference in Washington, D.C., on September 1, 2026.
